2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP

1	# andesim profile - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Finds the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in QEMU. For each detected loop you get the
5	loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, the iteration count, and a ready
6	`measure: --pc-start .. --pc-end ..` window you can paste into a hybrid
7	run. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
8	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
9	
10	Two parts ship together:
11	
12	- `qemu_plugin/hotIterationLoop.c` - QEMU TCG plugin
13	  (`libhotIterationLoop.so`) that records edges.
14	- `andesim profile` - the driver command that picks the engine, launches
15	  QEMU with the plugin, and formats the report.
16	
17	## Usage
18	
19	```
20	./andesim profile [--engine <id>] [options] <elf> [-- <extra qemu args>]
21	```
22	
23	profile is engine-synced, exactly like hybrid: it picks a cycle-accurate
24	engine (`--engine <id>`, or the sole installed one) and derives the QEMU
25	launch from it -- the `-cpu` model from the engine's `--print-qemu-config`
26	probe, `vlen` from its `--describe`, and the probe's config staged as
27	`-readconfig`. So the profile sees the same ISA the engine will measure:
28	a different `vlen` changes `vsetvl` trip counts, which changes the loop
29	ranking itself.
30	
31	If the engine does not answer `--print-qemu-config`, profile warns and
32	falls back to the family-default `-cpu` (the report may then not match
33	the engine's ISA).
34	
35	### Options
36	
37	| Flag                | Default   | Description                                                    |
38	|---------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
39	| `--engine <id>`     | sole one  | The engine whose QEMU config to profile on (`./andesim list engines`). |
40	| `--limit <N>`       | 50        | Print at most N loops.                                         |
41	| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1         | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
42	| `--optimize-rvv`    | on        | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
43	| `--no-optimize-rvv` | -         | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
44	| `--llm`             | on        | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
45	| `--no-llm`          | -         | Emit the plain human-readable table instead.                   |
46	| `--no-source`       | off       | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
47	| `--objdump <bin>`   | auto      | Override objdump (default: `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`'s riscv objdump). |
48	| `--addr2line <bin>` | auto      | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
49	| `--raw`             | off       | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
50	| `--mem-size <spec>` | QEMU dflt | Guest RAM, forwarded as QEMU `-m`.                             |
51	| `--dry-run`         | off       | Print the exact QEMU command and exit, running nothing.        |
52	| `-- <args...>`      | -         | Everything after `--` is forwarded verbatim to QEMU.           |
53	
54	The old standalone `build/hotloops` tool and its QEMU-shape flags
55	(`--arch`, `--qemu`, `--plugin`, `--machine`, `--cpu`, `--qemu-config`,
56	`--cwd`, `--qemu-arg`) are gone: the engine and `config.env` decide the
57	QEMU shape now, and extra QEMU args ride the `--` passthrough.
58	
59	### Build prerequisites
60	
61	The plugin lives in `qemu_plugin/`. Build once:
62	
63	```
64	make -C qemu_plugin
65	```
66	
67	It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotIterationLoop.c`. The QEMU
68	binaries themselves do **not** need to be rebuilt.
69	
70	## How it detects a loop
71	
72	For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
73	instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
74	remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
75	The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
76	iterations.
77	
78	This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
79	goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
80	semantics.
81	
82	Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
83	that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
84	on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.
85	
86	## Output modes
87	
88	Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:
89	
90	1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
91	2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
92	3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).
93	
94	### LLM report (default)
95	
96	The command emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
97	reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
98	first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.
99	
100	Layout:
101	
102	- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
103	  `rvv_filter`.
104	- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
105	  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
106	  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
107	- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
108	  - `iters`.
109	  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff` at the loop's header and tail).
110	  - `measure` - a ready `--pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>` pair
111	    covering the loop's whole enclosing function (entry -> ret). Paste it
112	    straight into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`.
113	  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
114	    tail map to different lines).
115	  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
116	    in DWARF.
117	  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
118	    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
119	  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
120	    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
121	    same-function nesting.
122	  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
123	    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
124	    show as `(indirect)`.
125	
126	The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
127	no LLM call is made by the command itself.
128	
129	Limitations:
130	
131	- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
132	  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
133	  `calls:` to bridge.
134	- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
135	  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
136	  fall back to just `file:line`.
137	- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
138	  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
139	  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.
140	
141	### Table mode (`--no-llm`)
142	
143	Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:
144	
145	```
146	# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
147	iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
148	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
150	...
151	```
152	
153	Columns:
154	
155	- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
156	- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
157	- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
158	- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
159	                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
160	                FUNC symbol.
161	- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
162	                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
163	                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
164	                info and `--no-source` is not set.
165	
166	### Raw mode (`--raw`)
167	
168	Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
169	plugin output:
170	
171	```
172	hotIterationLoop: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
173	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
174	0x..., 0x..., <n>
175	...
176	```
177	
178	Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.
179	
180	## Example
181	
182	A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:
183	
184	```c
185	/* profile_demo.c - baremetal entry */
186	#include <stdint.h>
187	
188	__attribute__((noinline))
189	static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
190	    int s = 0;
191	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
192	    return s;
193	}
194	
195	void main(void) {
196	    static int a[64], b[64];
197	    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
198	    long total = 0;
199	    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
200	        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
201	    (void)total;
202	}
203	```
204	
205	Build it against the vplat runtime (USER_GUIDE section 4), then run:
206	
207	```
208	$ ./andesim profile --min-iters 100 --limit 5 profile_demo.elf
209	```
210	
211	LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:
212	
213	```markdown
214	# HotIterationLoop Report
215	target:           profile_demo.elf
216	total_iters:      32000
217	reported_loops:   1
218	min_iters:        100
219	rvv_filter:       on
220	
221	## TL;DR
222	Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (profile_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
223	total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
224	(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.
225	
226	## Loops
227	
228	### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
229	iters:        31500
230	function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
231	measure:      --pc-start 0x80000200 --pc-end 0x80000230  (all of dot_rvv: entry -> ret)
232	source:       profile_demo.c:6
233	code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
234	rvv:          yes (4 insns)
235	rvv_insns:
236	  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
237	  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
238	  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
239	  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
240	parent:       -
241	children:     []
242	calls:        []
243	```
244	
245	Reading the report:
246	
247	- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
248	  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
249	- The `measure:` line is the handoff to hybrid: run
250	  `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start 0x80000200
251	  --pc-end 0x80000230 profile_demo.elf` to get the cycle figure for all
252	  of `dot_rvv` on the same engine the profile ran against.
253	- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
254	  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
255	  of branching back).
256	- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
257	  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
258	  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar

260	
261	For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:
262	
263	```
264	$ ./andesim profile --raw profile_demo.elf | head
265	hotIterationLoop: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
266	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
267	0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
268	```
269	
270	## Tips
271	
272	- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
273	  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
274	  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
275	- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
276	  to see the full distribution.

4	# the sole one) and derives the QEMU launch from it: -cpu from the engine's
5	# `--print-qemu-config` driver globals, vlen from its --describe, the staged
6	# qemu.cfg as -readconfig. Layers:
7	#
8	#   1. unit (fast, pure): the profile core (parse/filter/nest/render/argv)
9	#      plus the CLI parse of the profile flags.
10	#   2. fake engines (no real vsim, no QEMU): throwaway engine scripts that
11	#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real
12	#      discover -> resolve -> probe -> argv path; --dry-run prints the exact
13	#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.
14	#   3. real engine (guarded): the probe/argv against a built sim_* binary,
15	#      still --dry-run (the full QEMU run is covered by
16	#      tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh).
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
22	
23	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

27	# 1. unit: profile core + CLI parse

31	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------

34

36	# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
37	# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
38	mkengine() {
39	  local f="$1/$2"

41	#!/bin/sh

findings.title: profile silently ignores run-only flags --runtime and --step-timeout-ms, contradicting its own reject-loudly policy
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:241-263 declares 'reject run-only flags loudly instead of silently ignoring them' and rejects --mode/--trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end/--verify/--kanata/--gdb/--gdb-port/--print-memmap. But cli.cpp:111 and :116 parse --runtime and --step-timeout-ms for every subcommand, and grep shows both are consumed only by cmd_run.cpp (lines 186-804 for cli.runtime, 613 for cli.step_timeout_ms) - cmd_profile never reads them and never rejects them. So 'andesim profile --runtime linux app.elf' silently profiles the bare-metal app WITHOUT the vlinux proxy kernel (a different workload than the hybrid run the report's measure: windows target), and --step-timeout-ms is silently dropped. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh section 2g ('run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored') tests only --trigger/--mode/--verify, so the gap is untested.
findings.safety: This is a behavior gap, not a structural refactor - flagged for separate handling per instructions. The fix (two more rows in the runonly[] array at cmd_profile.cpp:247-257) only turns a silent ignore into exit 2 with the existing 'not a profile option' message; no passing use case changes because the flags currently do nothing under profile.
findings.verify_with: Add 'expect 2 "not a profile option" ... profile --runtime linux ...' and '... --step-timeout-ms 5 ...' lines to section 2g of tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh, then run that script.

findings.title: Engine-sync probe (--print-qemu-config -> stage cfg -> extract -cpu -> default fallback) is written three times
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:313-325 runs run_process({acc->bin_path, "--print-qemu-config"}, 5000), then stage_qemu_cfg(wd, probe), then qemu_cpu_from_cfg(probe.out) with a kDefaultQemuCpu fallback. run_plan.cpp:396-404 does the identical sequence (probe, stage_qemu_cfg, qemu_cpu_from_cfg; the kDefaultQemuCpu fallback applied at line 304). cmd_run.cpp:509-513 (--print-memmap path) runs the same probe a third time with its own inline success check that re-states stage_qemu_cfg's condition (spawn_failed/timed_out/rc==0, cf. run_plan.cpp:145). The 5000 ms timeout is a bare literal in cmd_profile.cpp:317 and cmd_run.cpp:510 while run_plan.cpp:109 names it kQemuCfgProbeMs in an anonymous namespace - the constant already exists but is not exported. A single helper next to stage_qemu_cfg in run_plan.{hpp,cpp} (probe bin -> {cfg_path, cpu}) would serve all three call sites and retire the duplicated timeout literal.
findings.safety: Pure extraction: the helper performs the same calls in the same order with the same 5000 ms timeout and the same empty-string fallbacks; each caller keeps its own warning/log wording. No argv token or diagnostic changes.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh (sections 2a/2c/2e assert the derived -cpu/-readconfig and the probe-failure fallback), tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_print_memmap.sh, tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_dry_run.sh, and build/driver unit tests (plan_test).

findings.title: cmd_exists()/find_first() re-implement the $PATH walk that cmd_doctor.cpp already has as which()
findings.detail: cmd_profile.cpp:51-68 (cmd_exists: split $PATH on ':', access(dir+"/"+cmd, X_OK); find_first: first existing candidate) duplicates cmd_doctor.cpp:125-141 (which(): same $PATH split + access X_OK, returning the full path, plus a !is_directory guard and trailing-'/' handling). Two independent PATH-resolvers in the same driver binary; cmd_exists(cmd) for a '/'-containing cmd is a one-line access() special case on top. Hoisting which() into a shared header (e.g. strutil.hpp or process.hpp) and expressing cmd_exists as a wrapper removes one implementation.
findings.safety: Behavior-preserving for all existing call sites: cmd_profile only ever asks about toolchain binary names (objdump/addr2line variants), for which the extra !is_directory guard in the doctor version is a strict-superset check that cannot flip a real executable from found to not-found; the '/'-path short-circuit stays in the wrapper. cmd_doctor keeps its exact which() semantics.

findings.title: Third hand-rolled mkdtemp scratch-dir implementation; also hardcodes /tmp unlike the other two
findings.detail: The driver has three mkdtemp implementations: tempdir.cpp:11-18 make_temp_dir() (fs::temp_directory_path + prefix-XXXXXX, the designated shared helper per tempdir.hpp:1-2), run_plan.cpp:368-379 (inline temp_directory_path + "andesim-plan-XXXXXX" + mkdtemp), and cmd_profile.cpp:216-231 (struct Workdir with the literal template "/tmp/andesim-profile.XXXXXX"). cmd_profile's copy is the only one that hardcodes /tmp, ignoring $TMPDIR, and tempdir.hpp's comment ('currently: --runtime linux's manifest staging') documents that the shared helper has only one consumer while two near-copies exist. Workdir's RAII remove_all is 3 lines on top of make_temp_dir(); run_plan already does its own remove_all at line 453.
findings.safety: Replacing both open-coded sites with make_temp_dir() keeps the same create-unique-dir semantics and each caller's existing cleanup. The only observable delta is cmd_profile's workdir moving from a hardcoded /tmp to the system temp dir (identical when $TMPDIR is unset, which is the tested configuration); no test asserts the /tmp prefix - test_andes_sim_profile.sh greps the staged cfg as '-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg', path-agnostic. findings.title: Plugin header comment says backward edge is 'strictly less than'; the code (and docs/profile.md) use <=
findings.detail: The file comment (lines 4-6) reads 'when the next executed translation block starts at a PC strictly less than the last instruction PC of the previously executed TB'. The actual test at line 75 is 'tbi->tb_start <= st->last_tail_pc' - equality included, which is what counts a one-instruction self-loop (a single-insn TB whose start IS its last-insn PC, e.g. 'loop: j loop' or a 1-insn vector-tail loop). docs/profile.md:72-74 documents the <= form ('starts at a PC `<=` that remembered PC'), so the in-file comment is the odd one out and misdescribes a deliberate boundary condition.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit ('strictly less than' -> 'less than or equal to (equality = a single-instruction self-loop)'); no code change, cannot alter behavior.
findings.verify_with: make -C qemu_plugin still compiles; tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh and build/driver/andesim-profile-test are unaffected by a comment.

findings.title: profile_qemu_argv hardcodes the AE350 QEMU boot tokens a third time, with drifted flag spellings
findings.detail: profile_qemu_argv (profile.cpp:426-448) hand-builds '-M andes_ae350 ... -nographic -semihosting -bios {elf}'. The same boot shape is hardcoded twice more in engine_registry.cpp's builtin qemu descriptor: the fast-leg template (lines 53-60) and the standalone template (lines 71-74), both spelled '-machine andes_ae350 ... -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios {elf}'. The spellings have already drifted (-M vs -machine; bare -semihosting [target=auto] vs -semihosting-config target=native), so a future machine/semihosting change must be found and made in three places. Minimal structural fix: align profile_qemu_argv's spellings with the descriptor's (-machine, -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native) and note the other sites in a comment; full unification (deriving profile's base argv from the builtin descriptor template) is a larger design change and NOT proposed here.
findings.safety: -M is a documented QEMU alias of -machine (identical parse). '-semihosting' means target=auto, which resolves to native exactly when no gdb client is attached - profile never passes -gdb/-S and cmd_profile rejects --gdb (line 254), so target=native is the value both spellings produce on every profile run. The exact-argv expectations in profile_test.cpp:198-226 must be updated with the same token strings (test-only edit, same commit).
